full_judgment:
2. This civil petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgment dated 11.3.2003 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2889 of 2002 making absolute the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated 23.5.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 82 of 2001 reversing those of dated 15.1.2001 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 270 of 2000 dismissing the suit. 

 6. As it appears the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit mainly on the ground that the order of termination was a termination simpliciter passed under Rule 57(B) of Chapter 7 of BOESL Employees Service Regulation giving him the service benefit and so there was nothing to be interfered with. But the appellate court decreed the suit relying on the decision reported in 47 DLR (AD) 66 and also upon exhibit 5, i.e. the minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors of the BOESL, which shows that although the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 termed the order of termination passed against the petition as termination simpliciter but from the contents of said exhibit it is clear that order of termination was in fact passed as a measure of punishment. However the High Court Division made the Rule absolute holding that the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 1 and 47 DLR (AD) 66 are quite consistent on the question of the legal and factual implication of an order of termination simpliciter and that though in paragraphs 6 and 8 of the plaint of the present suit allegations of malafide were made but the law requires that mere allegation of malafide is not enough and such allegation has to be substantiated by adducing evidence and further though in paragraphs 6 and 8 of the plaint the petitioner alleged conspiracy against him by as many as four persons, namely, Mr. Obaidul, General Manager, Mr. Shahidul Haque, Assistant General Manager (Foreign employment), Mr. Mosharraf Hossain, Manager (Foreign employment) and Mr. Enamul Haque, Manager Accounts of BOESL but none of them were made parties in the suit and no paper or document was filed to show their enmity with the petitioner of that they were instrumental behind the termination of the petitioner and moreover there is also nothing on record to show that at any point of time defendant No.2 or any other officers of BOESL acted against the petitioner on filed any complaint against him and further Ext.5, the minutes of the meeting of the Board of Directors of BOESL, was never communicated to the petitioner and that decision taken in Ext. 5, being an internal matter of the BOESL, the petitioner was not entitled to use the same to prove his case of malafide or to make out a case of camouflage by the respondent No.2 to pass an order of major punishment by way of terminating him from service; Ext.5 primafacie shows that the decision to terminate the petitioner from his service was taken by the Board of BOESL and when Board took the decision then how can it be said that it is the defendant No.2 who in a malafide manner took the decision to terminate the services of the petitioner as a measure of punishment particularly when the petitioner failed to produce any paper showing any pervious enmity or other bad feeling between him and the defendant No.2 and further Ext.5, on the face of it does not show that the decision to terminate the petitioner was taken as a measure of punishment and on the other hand it shows the decision to terminate the service of the petitioner was taken on other grounds and moreover Exhibit-4, the letter of termination, is a termination simpliciter without entailing any stigma on the petitioner and also without referring to any allegation made against the petitioner.
